lidar.source: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM, project GA_Statewide_2018_B18_DRRA (flown 2018, published 2022), tile USGS_1M_17_x40y371_GA_Statewide_2018_B18_DRRA.tif (public domain), from prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com. Not in the repo (351 MB): python3 tests/tools/lidar.py fetch --pin 33.494520,-82.023134 --download
lidar.located_by: a map pin from the project owner on the green (33.494520, -82.023134), placed at (8, 134) so the green the lidar shows (between its front bunker and the two behind) lands on the game green's centre (4, 138)

sand.why: the two back bunkers are small (5-7 yd) and sit at the foot of the bank behind the green: at the default 6 m smoothing they merge with the bank's toe into one 43 x 60 yd hollow; even at 2 m they stay joined to it, so they are placed by hand from the 2 m hollows (§8)

water.why: Rae's Creek is hydro-flattened at 48.93-49.0 m but too narrow for the automatic level; within 0.1 m it reads as a band 12-17 yd wide, its green-side shore 13 yd short of the pin, which is what the bridge photo shows
